boundaries: Rate, ratio and accounting identities only; projection models, life tables and stable-population theory are excluded.
Fertility/mortality aggregates over age groups are supplied inputs with stated scope, never computed from raw schedules here (no arrays).
Doubling time, half-life and any exponential or logarithmic form must be deferred with sources, never approximated.
Every rate states its reference population, period and scaling literal (per 1000 and similar) explicitly.
Expressions must be written in canonical base units of the runtime registry; never inline a conversion factor that belongs to unit scales (see the canonical-units rule).
coverage_guidance: Priorities are seeds, not a finite checklist. Continue into adjacent source chapters/subtopics inside the boundaries, selecting independently reusable relationships. Save multiple bounded batches without waiting for owner review. Check supplied inventory and prior returns for equivalent relationships and conflicting IDs. Record out-of-format discoveries as deferred with exact sources and missing capabilities; do not force chains or dilute quality for a quota.
integration_expectation: New meanings (crude_birth_rate, crude_death_rate, dependency_ratio, natural_increase and similar) and count/rate units require extension; all seed forms are scalar and fit the engine once meanings exist. Time aggregation stays in supplied period counts, never physical-time conversion.
mission: Curate atomic reusable algebraic demographic relationships: crude vital rates, age-structure ratios and population accounting balances, each with explicit reference population and period. Accounting arithmetic only; continue through successive batches with no inference chain required.
priorities: Crude birth and death rates from event counts and mid-period population
Total dependency ratio from youth, elderly and working-age populations
Population balance from births, deaths, immigration and emigration
Natural increase rate from crude birth and death rates
special_checks: Guard positive reference populations and nonnegative event counts; a zero population rejects, never divides
Keep rate scaling literals (1000, 100000) explicit in the expression with stated convention
Distinguish period counts from calendar dates; no date arithmetic is in scope
Distinguish the accounting identity from any causal or forecast claim
starter_sources: https://openstax.org -- navigate to a sociology or population-studies title and its chapters on population measures; record exact book, edition and section, never cite the root as evidence
No further source URLs were preverified for this assignment; discovery snippets alone do not prove the equation
